title: observability: token-level KV metrics, logging improvements, dashboard updates, and alert tuning
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: After the 2026-02-15 latency incident we lacked per-token visibility into KV cache behavior and related logging to correlate cache misses with downstream latency and cost. This PR adds token-level KV cache metrics, enhances logging for hot paths, updates Grafana dashboards to surface the new metrics, and tunes alert thresholds based on post-incident signal analysis. Summary of changes: 1) Runtime: instrumented token-level KV metrics (kv.token_hits, kv.token_misses, kv.kv_latency_p50/p95) and a lightweight histogram for per-request token-cost; 2) Logging: added structured JSON logs for KV lifecycle events (cache_lookup, cache_evict, cache_populate) with trace_id and token_count fields; reduced log noise by sampling at 0.1% for high-throughput routes and enabling full logs for error traces; 3) Dashboard: updated Token-Level Observability dashboard to include KV token hit/miss heatmap, per-model token-cost breakdown, and linked traces; 4) Alerts: adjusted existing token-cost and kv-miss alerts (raise thresholds for bulk-batch traffic, add a secondary alert with 10-minute window to catch persistent regressions); 5) Backwards compatibility: runtime metrics expose the old aggregated metrics unchanged; SDK and metrics consumers will see new metric names in addition to legacy ones; 6) Testing and rollout: unit and integration tests added, staged rollout to dedicated infra for 48h, final rollout after metrics validation. Migration notes: dashboards with saved views that referenced the old metric names will be auto-mapped; customers using self-hosted prometheus scrape configs should add kv.token_* metrics to allowed list. Rollout/monitoring plan: staged rollout on dedicated clusters, monitor kv.token_miss rate, per-model token-cost, and e2e latency SLO for 72h. Follow-ups: add sampling controls to config, add cost alerts per-customer, and run a synthetic load to validate long-tail behavior. Links: Incident SUP-4121 || Linear ENG-8342, ENG-8390 || Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/token-level-observability (internal) || Playbook update: docs/playbooks/kv-observability.md
commits_summary: - Add token-level KV metrics and histograms (instrumentation) - Add structured KV lifecycle logs with sampling - Update metrics exporter and Prometheus job to expose kv.token_* - Grafana: new panels for kv token heatmap and per-model cost breakdown - Alerting: tuned thresholds and added persistent regression rule - Tests: unit tests for metrics, integration test for end-to-end metric emission - Docs: playbook and upgrade notes
review_comments: Miguel Santos: Nice work. Two requests: reduce default log sampling to 0.1% for production routes and add a small perf benchmark to confirm instrumentation overhead <2%
Aisha Kapoor: Reduced sampling to 0.1% and added microbench in runtime/instrumentation/benchmark_kv.cpp; updated tests to assert no regression >2%
Lena Park: The alert thresholds look sane but please add an aged-alert to suppress noise for high-burst jobs
Aisha Kapoor: Added secondary alert rule with 10-minute aggregation window and noise suppression for known batch jobs (observability/alerts/kv_alert_rules.yaml)
Ethan Cole: CI flaked on integration test the first run, reran and passed. Approving after CI green.
release_notes: - Added token-level KV cache metrics (kv.token_hits, kv.token_misses, kv.kv_latency_p50/p95) - Structured KV lifecycle logs with sampling controls - New Grafana panels for KV token heatmap and per-model token-cost breakdown - Tuned alerts for token-cost and KV misses; added persistent-regression rule
